analysis.title: TransUnion (TRU): 3Q First Take: Revenue and margins outperform with the full year guide raised
key_insights: GS expects a positive investor reaction to TRU's 3Q 2026 release: revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS beat consensus, and full-year revenue and EPS guidance were raised.
3Q revenue was $1,312.5mn, up 12.2% y/y reported versus GS forecast of 11.5% and FactSet consensus of 11.8%. Organic constant currency growth was 7.6%, versus GS 7.3%, and down from 10.1% in 2Q.
Revenue grew 5.5% y/y OCC excluding FICO mortgage royalties.
US Markets revenue grew 6.8% y/y OCC, below GS 7.8%. Financial Services rose 10.8%, Emerging Verticals 5.6% and Consumer Interactive fell 3.0%.

International revenue rose 10.4% y/y OCC versus GS 5.4%, led by double-digit growth in Latin America and India, mid-to-high single-digit in Africa, Canada and the UK, and low-to-mid single-digit in APAC.

3Q adjusted EBITDA margin fell 90 bps y/y to 35.4%, in line with GS and consensus. The decline reflects a 60 bps drag from zero-margin FICO mortgage royalties and 40 bps of underlying contraction, partly offset by 10 bps from Mexico.
Full-year 2026 revenue guide moved from $5,127-5,162mn to $5,131-5,162mn, with OCC growth of 8-9% reiterated (5-6% excluding FICO royalties). EPS guide rose from $4.75-4.83 to $4.81-4.88.
FY2026 EBITDA margin guide is unchanged at 35.2-35.4%, down 60-80 bps, including flat to +20 bps of underlying expansion.
TRU expects 2026 US mortgage revenue to grow 28% with FICO royalties and 9% excluding them, despite an approximately 10% decline in mortgage inquiries.

4Q guidance midpoints are below GS and consensus on revenue ($1,264-1,294mn vs $1,288mn GS and $1,294mn consensus) and on EPS ($1.15-1.22 vs $1.20 for both). The EBITDA margin guide of 35.6-36.2% is below GS at 36.0% but above consensus at 35.8% at the midpoint.

GS rates TRU Neutral with a 12-month price target of $68 versus a $79.62 price, implying 14.6% downside. The target is 11.5x NTM+1YR EPS of $5.94, a discount to the Info Services peer median of 18.0x.

Call focus areas GS expects: consumer credit trends, the mortgage outlook with higher rates, VantageScore 4.0 adoption in mortgages, non-credit solutions performance, and tech transformation milestones.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $68 target, 14.6% below the $79.62 price, after a 3Q beat and raised full-year guidance. The multiple is set at a discount to peers for macro-sensitive transaction revenue and fintech and subprime exposure.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue $1,312.5mn vs GS est $1,304.2mn and FactSet consensus $1,307.7mn (reported 10/27).
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA $464.8mn vs GS est $461.6mn and FactSet consensus $462.7mn. Adjusted EBITDA margin 35.4% vs 35.4% for both estimates (reported).
3Q26 EPS $1.25 (reported) vs GS est $1.20 and FactSet consensus $1.21.
FY2026 guidance (company): revenue $5,131-5,162mn (low end raised from $5,127mn), EPS $4.81-4.88 (raised from $4.75-4.83), EBITDA margin 35.2-35.4% (maintained).
Pre-print FY2026 estimates: GS revenue $5,148mn, 35.3% EBITDA margin, EPS $4.81. FactSet consensus revenue $5,160mn, 35.3% margin, EPS $4.83. GS says guidance points to stable consensus.

4Q26 company guidance: revenue $1,264-1,294mn, EBITDA margin 35.6-36.2% (flat to +60 bps, with about 30 bps drag from FICO royalty and about 20 bps from M&A), EPS $1.15-1.22. GS 4Q estimates: revenue $1,288mn, margin 36.0%, EPS $1.20. Consensus: revenue $1,294mn, margin 35.8%, EPS $1.20.
The 2026 guide assumes about 4 percentage points of growth from acquisitions and about 3 percentage points from FICO mortgage royalties.
GS forecasts: FY2026E EPS $4.81, FY2027E $5.50, FY2028E $6.42. FY2026E revenue $5,147.8mn, FY2027E $5,584.4mn.
risk_factors: Downside: a macro and credit market downturn, mortgage origination volume declines, growth and margin dilution from M&A, FX headwinds and financial leverage.
Upside: a stronger economic backdrop, healthy international and emerging market growth, and traction in US emerging verticals.
Mortgage inquiries are expected to fall about 10% in 2026, with higher interest rates weighing on the mortgage outlook.
